alternate_greeting.guide: An alternate greeting to start the chat, different in situation or tone from the first message but equally in character. Do not speak or act for {{user}}. Actions between *asterisks* and dialogue between quotation marks.

creator_notes.guide: Notes for whoever uses the card (not sent to the model): what the character is about, usage recommendations and suggested settings.
creator_notes.label: Creator notes

description.guide: Character description: who they are, their appearance, background, traits and how they relate to others. Written in third person, using {{char}}.
description.label: Description

first_mes.guide: First message {{char}} sends when the chat starts. It must be in character, invite a reply and not speak or act for {{user}}. Actions between *asterisks* and dialogue between quotation marks.
first_mes.label: First message

image_reading.guide: Physical description of the character based on their image: apparent age, build, face, hair, eyes, skin, clothing and distinguishing features.
image_reading.label: Image reading

lorebook_description.guide: A short description of a lorebook: what world or topic it covers, what kind of entries it contains and which stories it is useful for. It is a note for its author (it is not sent to the model).
lorebook_description.label: Lorebook description

lorebook_entry.guide: The content of a lorebook entry: setting information (a place, object, faction, character, world rule…) written as concise, objective facts the model can use when its keywords come up. No dialogue and no instructions to the model.
lorebook_entry.label: Entry content

lorebook_entry_keys.guide: Keywords that trigger this entry: 3 to 8 short terms or names someone might use to refer to the topic in conversation (synonyms, nicknames, variants). Return them separated by commas, on a single line.
lorebook_entry_keys.label: Keywords

lorebook_entry_title.guide: A short title (2 to 6 words) that identifies this lorebook entry for its author.
lorebook_entry_title.label: Entry title

mes_example.guide: Dialogue examples that show the character's voice. Each example starts with a <START> line and alternates "{{user}}: …" and "{{char}}: …" lines.
mes_example.label: Dialogue examples

persona_description.guide: Description of the user's persona (their representation in the roleplay): appearance, personality and background, using {{user}}.
persona_description.label: Persona description

personality.guide: Concise summary of the personality: traits, quirks, way of speaking and values. It can be a short list of traits.
personality.label: Personality

post_history_instructions.guide: Brief instructions sent after the chat history to reinforce the style or the rules of {{char}}.
post_history_instructions.label: Post-history instructions

scenario.guide: Scenario: the situation, place and context in which the interaction between {{char}} and {{user}} begins.
scenario.label: Scenario

sd_background.guide: Stable Diffusion prompt describing a visual novel scene or background: place, era, lighting, time of day, mood and key elements as comma-separated English tags, e.g.: medieval library, candles, moonlight, wooden shelves, warm light. A single line, no people and no quality tags (those already live in the base style).
sd_background.label: Background prompt

sd_character.guide: Stable Diffusion prompt describing the character's FIXED physical appearance (hair, eyes, skin, features, build, usual clothes and accessories) as comma-separated English tags, e.g.: red hair, long hair, big eyes, freckles, white dress. A single line, no sentences, no proper name, no pose, background or quality tags (those already live in the base style).
sd_character.label: Character image prompt

stat_description.guide: Description of a visual novel stat: what exactly it measures, what low and high values mean and how it should influence the behavior, tone and decisions of the characters (or the world). It is sent to the AI as a rule, so be clear and concrete.
stat_description.label: Stat description

system_prompt.guide: This card's own system prompt: instructions on how the model should behave and write when playing {{char}}.
system_prompt.label: System prompt

world_description.guide: The premise of a visual novel world: place, era, tone, starting situation, conflicts and setting rules. It is sent to the AI as the story's scenario; do not write dialogue or decide what the user does.
world_description.label: World premise

prompts.image: Describe in detail the physical appearance of the character shown in the image: apparent age, build, face, hair, eyes, skin, clothing, accessories, posture and distinguishing features. Describe only what is visible; do not invent personality, name or backstory. Write in third person and in prose (one or two paragraphs), with no headings or lists. Write in English, unless the user's additional instructions are in another language: then use that language.
prompts.system: You are a writing assistant for roleplay character creators (SillyTavern-style character cards). You write and improve descriptions, personalities, scenarios, greetings and dialogue examples in a clear, evocative way that helps a language model portray the character well. Respect established facts, do not introduce contradictions, and use the {{char}} and {{user}} placeholders instead of proper names when natural. Write in the same language as the user's text or instructions (English by default). Reply only with the requested text: no preamble, no explanations, and do not wrap it in quotation marks or code blocks.

assistant.sd_image_prompt: Look at the image and write a Stable Diffusion prompt describing the physical appearance of the character shown: hair color and length, eyes, skin, features, build, visible clothes and accessories. English tags separated by commas, on a single line (e.g.: red hair, long hair, big eyes, freckles, white dress). Do not include the background, pose, expression or quality tags.
assistant.sd_system: You are an expert in Stable Diffusion prompts (anime and realistic models). You answer ONLY with the prompt: English tags separated by commas, on a single line, with no sentences, numbering, quotes or explanations. The data you receive may be in any language; translate it into tags.

prompt.analysis_system: You are the analyst of a visual novel. You read a scene and decide whether any stat changed. Reply ONLY with valid JSON, no extra text or markdown, in this shape: {"stats":[{"character":"<name>","stat":"<id>","change":<number>,"reason":"<short reason in {language}>"}]}. Changes are small (at most 25% of the range); most scenes change nothing: reply {"stats":[]}. Omit "character" for shared stats.
prompt.backgrounds_intro: Current background: {current}. Change the background (`scene.background`) only when the story moves to a new place.
prompt.choices_avoid:
Do not repeat or paraphrase these previous options; propose different alternatives:
{list}
prompt.choices_directive: [Now propose {user}'s options to continue the scene.]
prompt.choices_role: You are the writer of a classic visual novel (in the style of a dating sim). You propose the options {user}, the player, will choose from to decide how the story continues.
prompt.choices_rules:
# Rules
- Propose {count} options that differ from each other. Each one is what {user} would say or do next, written in the first person or as a short action (1–2 sentences).
- Each option must take the story down a different path (for example: kind, bold, cautious, funny, sincere), consistent with {user}'s personality, the characters in the scene, the situation, the location and the current stats (affection, trust…). Some may raise or lower those stats.
- Do not narrate the consequences, do not write for the other characters or the narrator, and do not use `[Name|expression]` tags.
- Write in {language}.
- Reply ONLY with valid JSON, with no markdown or extra text, in this shape: {"choices":["option 1","option 2","option 3"]}
prompt.control_background: - `scene.background`: the id or name of one of the available backgrounds.
prompt.control_intro: After the script, on its own line and exactly ONCE, add the block <vn>…</vn> containing valid JSON with only what changed. If nothing changed, write <vn>{}</vn>. Never mention or explain this block inside the script.
prompt.control_move: - `scene.enter` / `scene.exit`: lists with the names of cast characters who enter or leave the scene.
prompt.control_stats: - `stats`: list of `{"character": "<name>", "stat": "<id>", "change": <number>, "reason": "<short reason>"}` (omit `character` for shared stats). Every change is small: at most 25% of the stat's range.
prompt.directive_continue: [Continue the story: write the next scene.]
prompt.directive_start: [Write the opening scene of the story: set the place and the characters on stage, and end by leaving room for {user} to act.]
prompt.format:
# Output format (mandatory)
- One line per utterance: `[Name|expression] text`. Example: `[{example}|joy] “Welcome!”`.
- Narration goes as `[Narrator] text`.
- Only characters who are on stage may speak or act. Everyone else can only be mentioned in the narration.
- Never write {user}'s lines, actions, thoughts or decisions.
- Keep scenes short: 1 to 6 lines unless the story needs more. Stop when {user} has to respond.
- Write in {language} (the user's language), but keep the `[Name|expression]` and `[Narrator]` tags as they are.
- No headings or comments outside the script.
prompt.impersonate_draft:
Begin the message with the following text and continue naturally from it:
{text}
prompt.impersonate_role: You are {user}, the player of an interactive visual novel. You write what {user} says or does next.
prompt.impersonate_rules:
# Rules
- Write only {user}'s message, in first person or as a brief action; never write for the other characters or the narrator.
- Plain text, no `[Name|expression]` tags and no control blocks.
- Write in {language}, briefly (1–3 sentences).
prompt.offstage:
# Characters off stage
{names}. They do not speak or act until they enter the scene.
prompt.outfits_intro: Change a character's outfit (`scene.outfits`) only when the story calls for it.
prompt.role: You are the narrator and game master of an interactive visual novel. {user} is the player and you never control them. You write the next scene of the story as a script.
prompt.stat_world: - {name} (id: {id}; shared by the whole world; range {min}–{max}): {description}
prompt.stats_intro: They measure the state of the story and must be reflected in it.
prompt.stats_rule: Rule: low or high values MUST influence each character's behavior, tone and decisions where it makes sense (e.g. low affection: colder or refuses; high affection: warmer and closer). Do not mention the numbers in the script. Only propose changes in the control block when the events of the scene justify them: small changes and, in most scenes, none.
